title: Vivarium: 48 Species of Small Life Drawn in Code, for Godot 4
shortText: Butterflies, koi, frogs, fireflies and bats that fill your Godot 4 maps on their own: 48 species drawn in code.
html:
Vivarium for Godot 4: 48 species of small life drawn in code

Vivarium is a Godot 4.7 addon that fills your 2D maps with the small life a real place has: 48 species in 10 families (butterflies, moths, fireflies, dragonflies, bees, fish, frogs, bats, pond skaters and lizards), placed by reading your own TileMapLayer and changing with the time of day. Butterflies and bees work the meadow, dragonflies quarter the pond, koi move under the surface, frogs on the bank dive when your player walks up, lizards bask on the path, and at night moths circle the lamp, fireflies flash and bats hunt. No image file ships: every wing, fin and leg is drawn by GDScript into one texture when a level loads. A free MIT lite (12 species) is on this page. Royalty free in your games.

var life := Vivarium2D.new()
life.layers = [$Ground, $Water]   # your TileMapLayers
life.biomes = ["meadow", "pond"]
life.watch = [$Player]             # creatures flee from it
add_child(life)

Nothing to place

Vivarium2D reads each tile: a vivarium custom data value (water, ground, none) or, with no value, the tile's collision polygon (a wall or a tree trunk holds nothing). Water cells get fish under the surface, skaters on it and dragonflies over it; the bank gets frogs; open ground gets butterflies, bees and lizards. It fills what is on screen and keeps it filled as the camera moves. 8 biomes decide the cast (meadow, forest, pond, marsh, town, desert, cave and none), and VivariumZone2D marks habitat on maps that are not TileMapLayers.

Day, dusk and night

Set an hour, or let Vivarium read the colour of your CanvasModulate: a warm tint is dusk, a dark one is night, and the cast changes with it. Fireflies glow on their own layer above the night instead of being darkened with the ground.

48 species, 10 families

  • Butterflies (10): Cabbage White, Brimstone, Orange Tip, Red Admiral, Peacock, Common Blue, Swallowtail, Monarch, Blue Morpho, Small Copper. They flutter between flowers and settle with their wings opening and closing.
  • Moths (6): Buff tip, Garden Tiger, Luna Moth, Silver Y, Emperor Moth, Rosy Maple Moth. They flutter harder and circle the player at dusk and night as if they carried a lamp.
  • Fireflies (4): Meadow Firefly, Amber Firefly, Blue Ghost, Glow worm. They drift low and flash in their species' rhythm; each species falls into step and flashes together.
  • Dragonflies and damselflies (5): Emperor Dragonfly, Scarlet Darter, Golden ringed Dragonfly, Banded Demoiselle, Azure Damselfly. They dart and hover over the water, wings a blur.
  • Bees and hoverflies (4): Honeybee, Bumblebee, Hoverfly, Carpenter Bee. They zigzag from flower to flower.
  • Fish (6): Kohaku Koi, Showa Koi, Golden Orfe, Minnow, Pike, Perch. They glide under the surface and never leave the water; minnows swim in shoals.
  • Frogs and toads (5): Common Frog, Marsh Frog, Common Toad, Poison Dart Frog, Red eyed Tree Frog. They sit and croak on the bank and hop; walk up to one and it dives, leaving a ripple, and surfaces elsewhere.
  • Bats (3): Pipistrelle, Long eared Bat, Fruit Bat. They swoop in wide arcs.
  • Pond skaters and whirligigs (2): Pond Skater, Whirligig Beetle. They push and glide across the surface; whirligigs spin.
  • Lizards (3): Green Lizard, Leopard Gecko, Blue tailed Skink. They bask in the open, scuttle in short bursts, and dash off and freeze when the player comes close.

Every species is its own shape and pattern, not a recolour. Colours, size and count are parameters you move.

Hand placed too

VivariumColony2D puts one species exactly where you want it (a swarm of fireflies in a cave, koi in a palace pond, a bat roost). Each of the 48 species ships as a ready colony preset scene.

Both renderers, tested

Every species photographed by our pack gate under Forward+ and Compatibility (the renderer web exports use): 48 + 48 frames, zero engine errors, all 48 distinct. Creatures are plain 2D draw calls on one baked texture. Godot 4.7.2; older versions were not run and are not claimed. Orthogonal TileMapLayers; isometric and hexagonal layers were not tested.

Free lite on this page

Vivarium Lite is free (MIT): 12 of the 48 species (from the 5 families butterfly, firefly, dragonfly, fish, frog), the same Vivarium2D and colony nodes, and the demo.

Install

Copy addons/vivarium into your project. No plugin to enable. Open the godot folder as a project and press Play to see the field guide, a meadow by day, at dusk and at night.

Licence

Royalty free in your games, commercial use, no credit required. Edit and recolour freely. You may not resell or redistribute the files as an asset pack, addon or template. Plain language LICENSE.txt included.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the scripts, the species painters and the demo were written with AI, and the cover was made by an AI image model; every creature is drawn by that code at runtime.
